levels.title: Level 0 · Reading YAML
levels.summary: Every Kubernetes file is written in YAML. Start here if YAML is new to you.

lessons.title: Read a YAML file
lessons.summary: Learn the three rules of YAML and spot the most common indentation mistake.

levels.title: Level 1 · Kubernetes basics
levels.summary: Build each file one block at a time. Practise Anywhere lessons free on your laptop.

lessons.title: Run one container
lessons.summary: A Pod runs one or more containers together. It is the smallest thing Kubernetes runs.

lessons.title: Keep your app running
lessons.summary: A Deployment keeps the number of Pods you ask for running and replaces any that fail.

lessons.title: Group your work
lessons.summary: A Namespace keeps related objects together and apart from everything else in the cluster.

lessons.title: Give your app an address
lessons.summary: A Service gives a group of Pods one stable name and address inside the cluster.

lessons.title: Settings outside the image
lessons.summary: A ConfigMap holds settings, so you can change them without rebuilding the container image.

lessons.title: Passwords and keys
lessons.summary: A Secret holds passwords and keys apart from normal settings, so you can limit who reads them.

lessons.title: Run a task to the end
lessons.summary: A Job runs a task until it finishes. A CronJob runs a Job on a schedule.

lessons.title: Scale with load
lessons.summary: Add or remove Pods as CPU use goes up or down. Needs metrics-server installed.

lessons.title: Open your app to the internet
lessons.summary: EKS Auto Mode creates an AWS Network Load Balancer in front of your Pods.

lessons.title: Route web traffic
lessons.summary: EKS Auto Mode creates an AWS Application Load Balancer that routes web requests to your app.

lessons.title: Keep data after restarts
lessons.summary: EKS Auto Mode creates an Amazon EBS volume, so your data survives when a Pod restarts.

lessons.title: Let a Pod call AWS safely
lessons.summary: Give a Pod its own AWS permissions through an IAM role, without storing access keys.

levels.title: Level 2 · Tools
levels.summary: Short, explained files for Argo CD and Prometheus. Open them in the builder.

lessons.title: Deploy an app from Git
lessons.summary: Argo CD reads your files from Git and keeps the cluster matching them.

lessons.title: Set limits for your apps
lessons.summary: Choose which Git repositories and namespaces your Argo CD apps may use.

lessons.title: Collect metrics from your app
lessons.summary: Let Prometheus find your app and collect its metrics.

levels.title: Level 3 · Going further
levels.summary: More advanced templates and tool installation.

lessons.title: One app per environment
lessons.summary: Create one Application for each environment, such as dev and staging, from one template.

lessons.title: Add a scrape job
lessons.summary: Tell Prometheus to collect metrics from one fixed address.

lessons.title: Get an alert
lessons.summary: Get an alert when a problem lasts longer than the time you choose.

lessons.title: Install Argo CD or Prometheus
lessons.summary: Install a tool on your cluster with tested, explained settings.
